pairs.question: Qui tantam bestiam percussisset?
pairs.derivation: Reported exchange in the L. Domitius anecdote: a herdsman runs up to the praetor expecting reward. The speech tags 'quaesisse Domitium' (he asked) and 'illum respondisse' (the other replied) are framing/narration and are dropped; the remaining words are the author's own utterances. The question 'qui tantam bestiam percussisset' (who struck so great a beast) is presentation-normalized to a freestanding interrogative; the answer 'venabulo' (with a hunting-spear) genuinely answers it. Stops before the narrative continuation 'statim deinde iussu praetoris in crucem esse sublatum'.

pairs.question: Ipse autem triumphus quam ob rem omnium triumphorum gratissimus populo Romano fuit et iucundissimus?
pairs.answer: Quia nihil est victoria dulcius, nullum est autem testimonium victoriae certius quam, quos saepe metueris, eos te vinctos ad supplicium duci videre.
pairs.derivation: Cicero poses the question (why was the triumph the most pleasing of all triumphs to the Roman people?) and immediately answers it himself with 'Quia...' The answer is taken as the single sentence to the first full stop; nothing follows that sentence within the rhetorical unit. No scaffolding inside either span.
